name: Shiki
tagline: Terminal colours that drift slowly with local sunrise, sunset and the seasons, with continuous contrast safety.
description: Most terminal themes snap abruptly between a blinding noon white and a pitch-black midnight toggle. Shiki lets your terminal paper and ink breathe with the real sky outside—drifting imperceptibly from cool dawn mist to warm afternoon paper, amber dusk, and deep indigo night.

Driven by local solar elevation and the four seasons, shiki-term interpolates a continuous palette gradient while mathematically clamping every foreground and ANSI accent token against WCAG contrast floors so long coding sessions never sacrifice legibility for atmosphere.

features.title: Continuous solar elevation gradient
features.detail: Computes local sunrise, solar noon, twilight, and midnight offline from latitude or timezone—eliminating jarring binary light/dark switches.

features.title: Four-season ink & paper undertones
features.detail: Shifts palette warmth gently across spring sakura paper, crisp summer cedar, autumn persimmon dusk, and quiet winter sumi.

features.title: Guaranteed WCAG contrast floor
features.detail: Continuously verifies relative luminance across every interpolated stop, clamping body text and syntax tokens to AAA-grade contrast (>= 7:1).

features.title: Live OSC escape sequences for modern terminals
features.detail: Updates Ghostty, Kitty, WezTerm, Alacritty, and iTerm2 palettes smoothly in place via standard terminal OSC colour sequences.

install.label: CLI preview
install.note: In development — CLI daemon and one-shot shell hook preparing for first public beta.
